Once there were sitewide movements to organize and inform people how to get in touch with their representatives if the government tried passing laws that the EFF found draconian.

Now they would probably consider listing a congressman's office number and public email "doxxing", while letting said congressman know what you as a constituent want from your representatives count as "harassment".
The unforgivable thing to me is how the site was effectively neutered in regards to protesting or even discussing the various trade treaties and fast track legislation.
Hello and welcome! Doxxing is not allowed here as well... just sayin'. The word is not such a huge blanket though, probably.

One of the most important things reddit ever did was organize against SOPA.

The TPP happened without any mainstream reddit coverage.

I don't think listing the publicly available number for a public servant should EVER be considered doxxing.

That's political censorship plain and simple.

Oh, yeah, i'm totally anti-doxxing. Anonymous speech without fear of being outed and targeted is covered under the first amendment as far as I'm concerned.

I'm just miffed that some of the most egregious legislature ever is getting passed without the organized online opposition we were once able to muster.
